svg.title: Jing-Zhang City Completeness v0.6 Inclusion and Burden Matrix
svg.desc: Nine design personas showing public benefit, burden and exclusion risks, non-AI equivalent paths, and human-help or appeal requirements. Personas are design-review tools, not demographic facts.
svg.text: v0.6 | Inclusion and burden: who benefits, who bears cost, who can opt out
Nine personas are design-review tools, not population statistics. No AI enhancement may turn “no phone, no account, no tracking, or need for human help” into loss of basic city services.

g.text: Design persona
Primary public benefit
Potential burden / exclusion risk
Non-AI equivalent path
Human help / appeal
1 Long-term residents / families
Short daily trips, care, civic commons
Stable service rather than one-off spectacle
Neighborhood becomes a testbed; noise; privacy spillover
Ordinary housing, shops and community services continue
Staffed community desk; public stop/correction route
2 Older residents
Care access, rest, clear wayfinding
Digital barriers, misdirection, service moved into an app
Fixed signs, phone/in-person help, places to sit and rest
Priority human review; user or carer may appeal
3 Disabled / sensory-limited users
Continuous access, understandable info, independent arrival
AI personalizes the wrong route; physical barriers get hidden
Physical accessibility exists before digital enhancement
Accessibility review; wrong route corrected immediately
4 Children and carers
Childcare/learning, safe slow movement, family routines
Unneeded profiling, over-automation, testing mixed with children
Human care, physical safety boundaries, ordinary play space
Carer informed; high-risk tests default away from child routes
5 Students / researchers
Learning, shared equipment, research-to-city translation
Account lock-in, research-data overreach, exclusion by price
Open catalog, staffed booking, offline learning/exchange
Human review; IP/data disputes escalated to accountable roles
6 Founders / enterprise workers
Testing, translation, enterprise services, adoption
Public resources become closed channels; commitments overstated
Open admission rules, staffed enterprise service, non-AI process
Admission/exit rules public; conflicts handled by people
7 Service workers / commuters
Reliable arrival, rest, staffed help, ordinary jobs
Automation shifts labor burden, waiting, movement risk
Normal shifts, human jobs and commute routes stay available
On-site staff; work/mobility issues can be escalated
8 Visitors / international users
Multilingual arrival, heritage understanding, public exchange
Translation error, default consent, local-app-only service
Chinese/English fixed signs + staffed advice + no-account access
Multilingual correction; misinformation can be reported
9 No-phone / no-account / opt-out users
Full right to city use and public service
Digital exclusion, default consent, worse treatment after opt-out
L1/L2 permanent signs, staffed entry, paper/in-person process
No explanation required to refuse AI; equal human appeal

svg.text: Shared rule: every persona retains the non-AI baseline. Refusing tracking/registration or an AI shutdown must not reduce housing, movement, basic public services, or access to public space.
